samples.summary: The new slides numeric band exists only on the v1 REST `PUT`; the collaborative Yorkie path reads/writes slide text bodies unbanded
samples.evidence: `bandSlideBlockNumerics` / `bandSlideCellNumerics` / the inline `fontSize` band were added to `assertValidSlidesBody` (`packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:1001-1078`), whose own doc-comment says a slide text body "passes through no attribute codec" so the band must happen on write. But the REST endpoint is not the only writer or reader: `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:494-512` materializes a text element as `data: { ...extras, blocks }` with `blocks = yorkieToPlain(data.blocks)` — no `normalizeFontSize` / `normalizeTableSpan` / `normalizeRowHeight` anywhere in that file — and the slides editor writes bodies straight back through the same store. A peer (or any client) writing `fontSize: 1e9` or `rowSpan: Infinity` into `el.data.blocks` never passes the controller, and those blocks are fed to the shared docs layout (`computeLayout`, docs `initializeTextBox`, `expandCellRangeForMerges` for cell selection). Unlike docs, where the same band is duplicated at both read boundaries (`crdt-tree.ts` and `yorkie-doc-store.ts`), slides has no read-side copy. The fix belongs on the slides read boundary, not on the new controller code.

samples.summary: PPTX importer is a producer of `fontSize`/`lineHeight` into verbatim-stored slide bodies and was left unbanded, while the DOCX importer was banded for exactly that reason
samples.evidence: The diff bands the DOCX importer (`packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts`) with the argument that "the importer is a *producer* of them, so it has to agree". The sibling importer was not updated: `packages/slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:489` (`style.fontSize = ctx.defaultFontSize * fontScale`), `:521` (`style.fontSize = (sz / 100) * fontScale`) and `:327` (`style.lineHeight = v / 100_000`) write straight from untrusted PPTX XML into slide text bodies that are persisted verbatim and never pass the new controller band (the import runs client-side via `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/pptx-actions.ts`). Out-of-band values from an imported deck therefore reach the docs layout unbanded.

samples.summary: The paste sanitizer was banded for fontSize/lineHeight/padding/rowHeights/image but still admits any finite column ratio and any finite cell span
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:333` still does `columnWidths.push(asNumber(rawWidths[c]) ?? 1 / cols)` — `normalizeColumnRatio` / `MAX_COLUMN_RATIO` are imported nowhere in this file — and `:290-293` keeps `colSpan`/`rowSpan` as any finite `Math.trunc(n) > 1` without `normalizeTableSpan`. Both fields are now banded at both CRDT read boundaries (`crdt-tree.ts` `parseColumnWidthsAttr`, `treeNodeToCell`) and in the slides controller, so a pasted `columnWidths: [1e9]` renders one way for the pasting client and another for every peer/reload — the producer/reader divergence the rest of the change closes. (`normalizeTableMerges` at `model/types.ts:726` clamps the spans to the grid, so the ratio is the live gap.)

samples.summary: `parseColumnWidthsAttr` drops a poisoned ratio (shifting later columns and shrinking `numCols`) while the slides controller keeps its index as `0` — two policies for the same field
samples.evidence: `parseColumnWidthsAttr` does `if (ratio === undefined) continue;`, so a `cols` string like `1e400,0.5` yields `[0.5]` and `computeTableLayout`'s `numCols = columnWidths.length` (`packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:153`) becomes 1 — every later column of every row silently stops rendering and the surviving cells shift left. The slides arm of the same change deliberately does the opposite (`.map((ratio) => normalizeColumnRatio(...) ?? 0)`, "so every later column keeps its index"). The two read boundaries for the same stored field now disagree about column identity.

samples.summary: New `MAX_IMAGE_SIZE` ceiling drops (rather than clamps) images, but the DOCX importer still writes unbounded EMU-derived pixel sizes
samples.evidence: `isPaintableImageSize` now also rejects any edge `> MAX_IMAGE_SIZE` (20000), and both CRDT readers drop the whole image when it fails (`packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:88-99`, `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:212-222`). `packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:215-221` writes `width/height = Math.round(emusToPx(ref.cx/cy))` with no ceiling, so a DOCX whose `<wp:extent>` exceeds it imports an image that renders once and then vanishes on the next read — and is erased from storage by any subsequent write-back. The diff banded this importer's `w:sz` and `w:line` as a producer for exactly this reason but left the image extents.

samples.summary: Board's Miro importer produces `fontSize` into docs Blocks without the new band
samples.evidence: `packages/board/src/import/miro/text.ts:128` copies `base.fontSize` from Miro JSON into `InlineStyle` with no `normalizeFontSize`. Board text elements are rendered through the docs layout, and (like slides) board content is not read back through the docs Tree codec, so this producer never meets the band the change installs at the docs read boundaries.

finding.summary: The new slides numeric band exists only on the v1 REST `PUT`; the collaborative Yorkie path reads/writes slide text bodies unbanded
finding.evidence: `bandSlideBlockNumerics` / `bandSlideCellNumerics` / the inline `fontSize` band were added to `assertValidSlidesBody` (`packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:1001-1078`), whose own doc-comment says a slide text body "passes through no attribute codec" so the band must happen on write. But the REST endpoint is not the only writer or reader: `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:494-512` materializes a text element as `data: { ...extras, blocks }` with `blocks = yorkieToPlain(data.blocks)` — no `normalizeFontSize` / `normalizeTableSpan` / `normalizeRowHeight` anywhere in that file — and the slides editor writes bodies straight back through the same store. A peer (or any client) writing `fontSize: 1e9` or `rowSpan: Infinity` into `el.data.blocks` never passes the controller, and those blocks are fed to the shared docs layout (`computeLayout`, docs `initializeTextBox`, `expandCellRangeForMerges` for cell selection). Unlike docs, where the same band is duplicated at both read boundaries (`crdt-tree.ts` and `yorkie-doc-store.ts`), slides has no read-side copy. The fix belongs on the slides read boundary, not on the new controller code.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The new bands exist only on the REST write path: bandSlideBlockNumerics (docs-content.controller.ts:1027-1057), bandSlideCellNumerics (:1060-1077) and the inline fontSize band (:1206) are called solely from assertValidSlideBlocks (:1114, :1134) under assertValidSlidesBody (:529), reached from the v1 PUT at :195; the function's own doc-comment (:1009-1019) states a slide body "passes through no codec at all" so the band must happen on write. The collaborative Yorkie path is a second, live entry point that neither bands on read nor on write: yorkie-slides-store.ts:493-511 returns data: { ...extras, blocks } from a raw yorkieToPlain, and withTextElement (:2210-2222), withTableCellText (:2683-2692) and withNotes (:2295-2299) write blocks back via clone() untouched. A repo-wide grep of packages/frontend/src for normalizeFontSize/normalizeTableSpan/normalizeRowHeight/normalizeCellPadding/normalizeListLevel matches only the docs store (yorkie-doc-store.ts:203, 326, 460-461, 487, 533), mirroring packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:86,195-196,230 — so docs bands at both read boundaries and slides at none. No compensating clamp downstream: normalizeBlockStyle (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:382-384) is a defaults spread, packages/slides/src has no such normalizers outside the PPTX exporter, and packages/backend/src/yorkie/slide-ops.ts does no banding. Reachable: the store backs slides-view.tsx / slides-detail.tsx / slides-presentation-mode.tsx and its blocks feed computeLayout via packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts and model/layout.ts. This is the lane's canonical case — a new guard with another entry point reaching the protected operation — and blocking at major severity.

finding.summary: HTML-paste path sets `fontSize` unbanded, bypassing the band this change added to the JSON-paste path in the same file
finding.evidence: `resolveInlineCSS` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:547-552) still does `style.fontSize = match[2] === 'px' ? (value * 72) / 96 : value` with no `normalizeFontSize`. The regex `^(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(px|pt)$` accepts `999999999px`, so pasting external HTML with `style="font-size: 999999999px"` puts ~7.5e8 pt on a run — the exact value the diff now refuses through `sanitizeInlineStyle` (clipboard.ts:166) precisely because "the pasting client [would render] something no peer will reproduce". `parseHtmlToInlines`/`parseHtmlToBlocks` are the primary paste route for anything copied from a browser, so the guard added in this file has a reachable way around it in this file. Fix belongs at clipboard.ts:551 (route through `normalizeFontSize`).

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that `resolveInlineCSS` assigns `style.fontSize` raw ("no `normalizeFontSize`"), leaving the HTML-paste route as a reachable bypass of the band added on the JSON route. That code is not present. At packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:547-561 the HTML path parses the px/pt match and then passes it through `normalizeFontSize(match[2] === 'px' ? (value * 72) / 96 : value)`, assigning only when the result is defined — the same helper the JSON path uses at clipboard.ts:166, imported at clipboard.ts:16. `normalizeFontSize` (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:111-115) drops non-finite/non-positive values and clamps to `MAX_FONT_SIZE`, so `font-size: 999999999px` is clamped, not stored as ~7.5e8 pt. Both callers of `resolveInlineCSS` (clipboard.ts:672 in the inline walker and clipboard.ts:772 in the block walker) go through that banded helper, and a grep of the file shows `fontSize` is assigned into an `InlineStyle` in only those two places (166 and 557), so no other unbanded HTML route exists. Ground: not-present.

mergedFrom.summary: DOCX import can produce a lineHeight above the new MAX_LINE_HEIGHT (20), which the reader now silently clamps

finding.summary: DOCX import writes font sizes above the new MAX_FONT_SIZE (400 pt); Word allows up to 1638 pt, so imported text is silently shrunk on the next read/reload
finding.evidence: `packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:50` does `style.fontSize = halfPointsToPoints(parseInt(val, 10))` with no clamp (and `parseInt` of a malformed `w:sz` yields NaN). Nothing on the import path passes `normalizeFontSize`; the value is written into the CRDT (`YorkieDocStore.setDocument` → `attrs.fontSize`), and every *read* now bands it — `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:200` and `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:82`. Result: a legitimate Word document with a 1638 pt (or any >400 pt) title renders at the imported size during the import session and at 400 pt for every peer and after reload, and a docx→docx round trip loses the size. A NaN `w:sz` is dropped on read but renders as NaN geometry locally. Either clamp at import or raise MAX_FONT_SIZE to the OOXML ceiling.

verdict.reason: The claimed missing clamp exists. packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:65 wraps the imported w:sz in normalizeFontSize (imported at line 8), and drops undefined results at line 66, so a malformed w:sz never writes NaN. The finding's quoted line 50 does not exist as described (line 50 is the underline branch). The finding also misstates the band: readers apply MAX_FONT_SIZE = 4000 (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:73), deliberately above Word's 1638 pt ceiling per the module note at lines 36-40; the 400 value is FONT_SIZE_MAX in packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-catalog.ts:86, a picker-only UI ceiling consumed by font-size-picker.tsx:72,102, not by any reader of stored attrs. Both cited readers (frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:203, docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:86) use normalizeFontSize, i.e. the same 4000 band the importer applies, so a 1638 pt title round-trips unchanged. Tests assert exactly this at packages/docs/test/import/docx-style-map.test.ts:328-341.

finding.summary: Slides text bodies reach the same docs layout sink with no band at all — the new numeric bands only exist in the docs Tree codec, which slides never pass through
finding.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks`/`assertValidTextBodyBlocks` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:976-1049) validate `style` via `assertValidBlockStyle` (finite block-style numbers only) and `normalizeSlideInlines`, and never look at inline `fontSize`, cell `padding`, `tableData.rowHeights` or `listLevel`. Slides roots are persisted verbatim JSON (`writeSlidesRoot`) and read back with no attribute codec, yet the slides renderer feeds those same blocks to the docs engine: `packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:239` calls `computeLayout` from `@wafflebase/docs`. So a `PUT` (or a PPTX import) carrying `fontSize: 1e9`/`padding: Infinity` inside a deck's text body reaches exactly the sink `model/numeric-attrs.ts` was written to protect, unbanded — the docs-side band gives no coverage here. The diff's own slides note only covers `listLevel` (via the exporter), not the sizes.

verdict.reason: The slides validator in the same controller does band exactly the values the finding says are unbanded. `normalizeSlideInlines` bands each run's inline `fontSize` via `normalizeFontSize` (docs-content.controller.ts:1203-1209, imported at :52), and `bandSlideBlockNumerics` (:1027-1057) bands block `lineHeight` (:1031), `listLevel` (:1036), `tableData.rowHeights` (:1044) and `tableData.columnWidths` (count-capped at MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS plus `normalizeColumnRatio`, :1053-1055); `bandSlideCellNumerics` (:1060-1077) bands cell `padding` via `normalizeCellPadding` (:1064) and `colSpan`/`rowSpan` via `normalizeTableSpan` (:1073). These are wired into the slides walk: `assertValidSlideBlocks` calls `normalizeSlideInlines` and `bandSlideBlockNumerics` per block (:1113-1114) and `bandSlideCellNumerics` per table cell (:1134); that walk is reached from `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` (:998) ← `assertValidTextBody` (:950-959), which is invoked for each element's text body (:797), for table-cell bodies (:945) and for slide `notes` (:680) — all before `writeSlidesRoot` runs at :247. So a `PUT` carrying `fontSize: 1e9` or `padding: Infinity` inside a deck's text body is repaired at this boundary, not stored verbatim. The reviewer's line window (960-1049) and the greps they ran simply missed the helpers at 1027-1077 and 1203-1209, and the docs-side module even documents this slides-side application (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:239-242). Only `isPaintableImageSize` is genuinely not applied here, but that guard is a read-time drop in both renderers rather than a stored-value band, and it is not what the finding asserts.
